conviction_note: The print is the first after the Aug 6 accelerated approval of TUDRIQEV (RP1). The product only became commercially available Oct 1, after the Sep 30 quarter end, so the reported quarter is a zero-revenue opex quarter. The stock will trade on the first launch commentary from the 8:00 ET call, and nothing public pre-signals that commentary. On one side: a crowded short (~25% of shares out, 12.7 days to cover), call-heavy options and an Iovance read-through that the post-PD-1 melanoma market is strong. On the other: a launch run on a commercial team cut in April, a +13% 5-day run-up into the call and an open automatic shelf. These roughly offset, so p_up is 51 on an abs_move of 8.0 (near the 8.87% option-implied move, above the 3.55% median history because this is the first launch call). The findings sum to +0.1 and the scaled number is +0.16, so the two measurements agree that there is no edge.
bar: Single source, so every finding is capped small. Benzinga's earnings-forecast page, as captured Aug 14 2026, shows a Q2 FY27 consensus of EPS -$0.76 and revenue ~$1.0M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/REPL/earnings-forecasts; WebFetch got a 403, so this is snippet_only). The +10% on EPS is my estimate. Q1 FY27 net loss was $69.8M on ~97M weighted shares (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1737953/000110465926096483/tm2623208d1_ex99-1.htm). The August raise added 9.7M shares plus 2.74M pre-funded warrants, and 94.2M shares were outstanding on Aug 11 plus ~16.8M pre-funded warrants (10-Q cover). So a similar ~$70-75M loss over ~108M weighted shares gives about -$0.66 to -$0.69. On revenue, the product launched Oct 1 (after quarter end), so revenue is likely ~$0 against ~$1.0M, which is immaterial in dollars. The company gives no numeric guidance.
positioning_check: Short interest 23,165,699 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement (23,128,025 on 09-30), avg daily volume 1.82M, 12.70 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/repl/shortinterest, fetched 2026-10-27). That is ~24.6% of the 94,219,634 shares outstanding on the 10-Q cover (Aug 11 2026), or ~20.9% including pre-funded warrants: a crowded short, stable at 22.8-23.5M since mid-August. The baseline shows 25d skew of -15.1 vol points (calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'), a put/call OI ratio of 0.11, ATM IV of 120% and an event-implied move of 8.87%. The ATM spread is 48% of mid, so the implied move is indicative only. Run-up is +13.3% over 5 days and -0.5% over 20 days. The stock is 19% below its 52-week high and +661% above its 52-week low.

findings.finding: The quarter being reported (Jul-Sep 2026) almost certainly carries ~$0 product revenue. TUDRIQEV was announced as 'now commercially available in the U.S.' on Oct 1 2026, after the Sep 30 quarter end, and the Aug 14 release said only 'will launch within 60 days'. The ~$1.0M revenue consensus (Benzinga, Aug 14 capture) is therefore stale-high by about $1M. The real content of the print is opex (Q1: R&D $49.3M, SG&A $19.0M, net loss $69.8M) and the first launch metrics from the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pre-revenue quarters have moved this name little. Baseline history: Aug 14 2026 (first print after approval, $0 revenue) -1.45%, Jun 29 2026 -3.70%, median |move| 3.55% over 7 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Anyone who reads the Oct 1 release knows the quarter had no sales. The only unpriced piece is the stale $1.0M revenue line in aggregator consensus, which no holder of a launch biotech trades on. If it mattered, a headline 'revenue miss' would already show up in preview copy, and none was found.
findings.independence: Same-direction document: the Aug 14 8-K exhibit says 'expects product in the market within 60 days' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1737953/000110465926096483/tm2623208d1_ex99-1.htm). The 10-Q income statement shows no product revenue through Jun 30.

findings.finding: The short base is crowded and sticky, and option flow leans upside. Short interest was 23.17M shares on Oct 15 (~24.6% of the 94.2M shares outstanding), with 12.7 days to cover, essentially unchanged since mid-August. Baseline options show put/call OI of 0.11 and 25d skew of -15 vol points. Any credible early-launch datapoint on the call (sites activated, patients treated, reimbursement in place) has a squeeze mechanism behind it. The +13% 5-day run-up suggests some of that is already being bought.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history for launch-metric surprises. On the Aug 6-10 approval and offering the stock reached a near-18-month high despite pricing $150M of equity at $12.06 (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/repl-stock-hits-near-18-month-high-on-pricing-of-150-m-offering-but-retail-sees-share-price-unwinding-over-time/cZojvWcRJOu). The Aug 14 print moved -1.45%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The skew and the 5-day run-up already show call buyers. What is not priced is that ~23M shares are still short at 12.7 days to cover into the first launch call. If shorts had been covering, short interest would have fallen from Aug-Sep levels, and it has not.
findings.independence: The baseline's options block (skew -15.1, P/C OI 0.11) is a different source pointing the same way. The 10-Q cover share count (94,219,634) is the denominator (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1737953/000162828026057099/repl-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: Iovance, maker of the direct competitor in post-PD-1 melanoma (Amtagvi), raised its 2026 revenue guide on Sep 29 2026 from $350-370M to $410-420M, citing sustained US demand and ~100 authorised treatment centers (110+ by year end). That is the first counterparty data point since Replimune last spoke on Aug 14. It shows the second-line melanoma pool is large and referring. It does not show whether an off-the-shelf intratumoral product takes share or adds to it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. This is the first launch quarter, so there is no history of the stock reacting to competitor read-throughs on a print.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy, and the market has had it for four weeks, so it is mostly priced. What it adds is a market-size anchor any early Replimune patient numbers will be judged against. Had the market read it as a share threat to Tudriqev, REPL would have fallen around Sep 29. Digrin shows September to October roughly flat to down ($13.24 to $11.75), which does not point either way.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The Iovance release does not mention Tudriqev. No Replimune document confirms how the two products interact.

findings.finding: The launch runs on a reduced commercial footprint. After the second CRL in April 2026 the company cut its workforce by 55%, and Q1 FY27 SG&A fell to $19.0M from $32.6M, partly attributed to a 'reduced commercial team'. The new CCO (Michelle DiNapoli) started only Aug 18. The first-call metrics (sites onboarded, patients dosed in ~4 weeks) are therefore at risk of looking slow against $600M-$1B peak-sales models.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior launch-metric print exists. On the Aug 14 print, which had commentary on launch preparation and the CCO hire but no metrics, the stock moved -1.45%.
findings.why_not_priced: The restructuring and SG&A cut are public. What is not priced is how they translate into week-4 launch numbers, which nobody outside the company has. If the market expected a slow start, the stock would not have run +13% in five days into the call, and calls would not be bid over puts.
findings.independence: Same direction: the Aug 14 8-K exhibit shows SG&A at $19.0M against $32.6M a year earlier (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1737953/000110465926096483/tm2623208d1_ex99-1.htm). Against it: the Cantor note cited on the same Quartr page says the launch 'targets rapid adoption in key accounts'.

findings.finding: An automatic shelf is open. Replimune filed an S-3ASR on Aug 14 2026, the same day as the Q1 release. With ~$70M of quarterly burn and runway stated only as 'greater than twelve months', a follow-on into any post-print strength is possible within the window. On what the money buys: the August raise ($141.0M net at $12.06) already funds the launch. Approval moved the Hercules maturity to Oct 2029 and opened up to $115M of further tranches. Going-concern doubt was removed in the 10-Q. So this is a supply overhang on an up-move, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the Aug 10 offering (9.7M shares plus pre-funded warrants at $12.06), the stock still traded to a near-18-month high, so the market has absorbed this issuer's equity supply before.
findings.why_not_priced: The shelf is public, and a biotech with ~$270M of estimated cash, ~$280M of annual burn and a fresh launch is widely expected to raise again. The unpriced part is only timing: a same-day or next-day deal would cap a pop inside the window. If the market expected a deal now, the stock would not be running into the print.
findings.independence: The 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1737953/000162828026057099/repl-20260630.htm) gives the Hercules terms and says going-concern doubt was 'subsequently alleviated'. That makes the financing a zero-to-small negative rather than distress.

outside_window.finding: Iovance reports Q3 2026 in early November, which will show whether Amtagvi demand slowed in the first month of Tudriqev's availability.
The next FINRA short-interest release (Oct 30 settlement), published around Nov 10.

rejected_candidates.detail: This is in the wire and is the same sell-side optimism the skew and run-up already reflect. It adds nothing that bears on this print beyond the positioning finding.

rejected_candidates.detail: Snippet only and not a primary document. It is used as the expectations context inside the reduced-footprint finding rather than filed on its own.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The crowded short and the call skew agree with each other and point up. The +13% 5-day run-up into a quarter with ~zero revenue, a lean commercial team and an open shelf point to sell-the-news. My evidence does not beat the options market's upside lean and does not contradict it, so p_up stays at 51.
lessons_applied: Rule 7: the two negatives run against a -15 call skew and a ~25% short base. The reduced-footprint finding went from -0.8 to -0.5 and the shelf from -0.5 to -0.3.

Rule 4: I asked what the money buys. The August raise funds a launched product, the Hercules maturity moved to 2029 and going-concern doubt was removed. The shelf stays a small supply-timing negative, not distress.
Rule 6: the bar has one source (a stale Benzinga capture), so every size stays small. The reported-quarter finding is left at -0.2.
Rule 5 / 8 tension: positioning was trimmed from +1.0 to +0.8, because the 5-day run-up suggests part of the squeeze is already bought. p_up moved from 50 to 51, abs_move unchanged at 8.0.
